To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) a practical ontology framework can be used to create ontologies and analyses for static model analysis of embedded software; (2) the framework can express infinite ontologies, including ontologies that are recursive; and (3) the framework can be applied to real-world use-cases in the avionics and automotive industries.
we have created a unified framework for the creation and use of ontologies in software analysis, and that we have shown how this framework can be applied to a range of use cases.
we have developed an ontology framework and associated analyses for static model checking, and we have shown how the framework can be applied to cyber-physical system domains.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a framework for static model checking that can be used to check that a software specification satisfies a correctness criteria expressed as an ontology.
the use of ontologies to provide domain-specific semantics to static model checking.
the use of ontologies to express domain knowledge and analyses over those ontologies to check software specifications against correctness criteria.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
we have presented a framework that is general, extensible, and applicable to many domains.
our approach is general, and that the patterns of infinite ontology that we present are applicable to many domains of interest.

our framework provides a means for the creation of ontologies that can be checked against software models, and that the ontologies that can currently be created are sufficient to express the domains of interest of cyber-physical systems, and that the analyses that can be run are sufficient to check the software that implements them.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
it enables users to express their domain knowledge in a way that can be used to check the software that implements it.
we present a practical framework for the analysis of static models with respect to ontologies.
we provide a framework to enable users to build ontologies for arbitrary domains, and then to run analyses over those domains.

we have developed a framework for the creation of ontologies and their application to static analysis of embedded software.
the use of domain-specific ontologies in the analysis of software models is a powerful and flexible technique that can be used in many different contexts.
